Jitter sf points by a fixed real-world radius, deterministically

Source: R/map_scale_bar.R
mysterymaps_jitter_points.Rd

Displaces each point in a random direction by up to miles, measured as a real ground distance (via EPSG:5070, meters) rather than a degree offset, so the same miles value means the same thing at every latitude. Jitter is deterministic by default: the same input and the same seed always produce the same output, which matters for a map that gets published and later needs to be regenerated identically.

Usage

mysterymaps_jitter_points(points, miles = 1.5, seed = 42)

Arguments

points

sf POINT layer.

miles

numeric(1): maximum jitter radius, in miles. 0 returns points unchanged.

seed

numeric(1) or NULL: seed for the jitter. Default 42, so jitter is reproducible out of the box; pass NULL to use the caller's current random stream instead (a different jitter each run).

Value

points, with jittered geometry, in its original CRS.

Details

Dot maps with physicians stacked on the same building or city block read as a single dot and understate the count there. A fixed, reproducible nudge pulls them apart without introducing run-to-run noise into a published figure. The seed is applied locally – the caller's .Random.seed is saved and restored on exit – so jittering one map does not reseed any later simulation in the same script.

Other mapping: mysterymaps_bivariate_choropleth_map(), mysterymaps_cartogram_map(), mysterymaps_catchment_redundancy_map(), mysterymaps_clear_isochrone_cache(), mysterymaps_create_isochrones(), mysterymaps_flow_map(), mysterymaps_hrr_maps(), mysterymaps_isochrones_for_df(), mysterymaps_map_acceptance_rate(), mysterymaps_map_acog_districts(), mysterymaps_map_base(), mysterymaps_map_block_group(), mysterymaps_map_leaflet(), mysterymaps_map_physicians(), mysterymaps_pathway_small_multiples_map(), mysterymaps_plot_isochrones(), mysterymaps_rate_choropleth_map(), mysterymaps_scale_bar()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
pts <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(lon = rep(-99.5, 3), lat = rep(40.2, 3)),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
mysterymaps_jitter_points(pts, miles = 1.5, seed = 42)
}
